A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hemodynamic abnormalities in the bicuspid aorta valve (BAV), such as the ones produced by the fusion of the left- and right-coronary cusps, promote endothelial activation, extracellular matrix degradation and osteogenesis, which are the hallmarks of calcific aortic value disease (CAVD).
BAV hemodynamics promote endothelial activation, fibroblastic and osteogenic differentiation, matrix remodeling and calcification, which may contribute to the development of BAV CAVD.
the hemodynamics experienced by the fused BAV leaflets are more likely to promote calcific degeneration of the valve than the hemodynamics experienced in TAVs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hemodynamic abnormalities associated with bicuspid aortopathy contribute to valvular calcific degeneration.
hemodynamic abnormalities are an important contributor to the early stages of calcific bicuspid aorto valve disease.
